Rule.rationale: Presence of the default SNMP password enables querying of different system aspects and could result in unauthorized knowledge of the system.

check.check-content: To ensure the default password is not set, run the following command: # grep -v "^#" /etc/snmp/snmpd.conf| grep 'public\|private\|snmp-trap\|password' There should be no output.

Rule.title: Ensure Approved Hash Is Used
Rule.description: Edit /etc/snmp/snmpd.conf, ensure every line beginning with createUser includes SHA, similar to the following: # createUser myuser SHA -l 0x0001020304050607080900010203040506070809 AES -l 0x00010203040506070809000102030405 Upon doing that, restart the SNMP service: # service snmpd restart
Rule.rationale: The SNMP service must use SHA-1 or a FIPS 140-2 approved successor for authentication and integrity.

check.check-content: To ensure SHA is used for SNMPv3 users, run the following command: # grep -v '^#' /etc/snmp/snmpd.conf | grep -i createUser | grep -vi SHA There should be no output.

Rule.title: Ensure Approved Encryption Is Used
Rule.description: Edit /etc/snmp/snmpd.conf, ensure every line beginning with createUser includes AES, similar to the following: # createUser myuser SHA -l 0x0001020304050607080900010203040506070809 AES -l 0x00010203040506070809000102030405 Upon doing that, restart the SNMP service: # service snmpd restart
Rule.rationale: The SNMP service must use AES or a FIPS 140-2 approved successor algorithm for protecting the privacy of communications.

check.check-content: To ensure AES is used for SNMPv3 users, run the following command: # grep -v '^#' /etc/snmp/snmpd.conf | grep -i createUser | grep -vi AES There should be no output.

Group.title: Documentation to Support DISA OS SRG Mapping
Group.description: These groups exist to document how the Red Hat Enterprise Linux product meets (or does not meet) requirements listed in the DISA OS SRG, for those cases where Groups or Rules elsewhere in scap-security-guide do not clearly relate.

Rule.title: Product Meets this Requirement
Rule.description: This requirement is a permanent not a finding. No fix is required.
Rule.rationale: Red Hat Enterprise Linux meets this requirement through design and implementation.

check.check-content: RHEL6 supports this requirement and cannot be configured to be out of compliance. This is a permanent not a finding.

Rule.title: Product Meets this Requirement
Rule.description: This requirement is a permanent not a finding. No fix is required.
Rule.rationale: The Red Hat Enterprise Linux audit system meets this requirement through design and implementation.

check.check-content: The RHEL6 auditing system supports this requirement and cannot be configured to be out of compliance. Every audit record in RHEL includes a timestamp, the operation attempted, success or failure of the operation, the subject involved (executable/process), the object involved (file/path), and security labels for the subject and object. It also includes the ability to label events with custom key labels. The auditing system centralizes the recording of audit events for the entire system and includes reduction (ausearch), reporting (aureport), and real-time response (audispd) facilities. This is a permanent not a finding.

Rule.title: Product Meets this Requirement
Rule.description: This requirement is a permanent not a finding. No fix is required.
Rule.rationale: Red Hat Enterprise Linux meets this requirement through design and implementation.

check.check-content: RHEL6 supports this requirement and cannot be configured to be out of compliance. This is a permanent not a finding.

Rule.title: Guidance Does Not Meet this Requirement Due to Impracticality or Scope
Rule.description: This requirement is NA. No fix is required.
Rule.rationale: The guidance does not meet this requirement. The requirement is impractical or out of scope.

check.check-content: RHEL6 cannot support this requirement without assistance from an external application, policy, or service. This requirement is NA.

Rule.title: Implementation of the Requirement is Not Supported
Rule.description: This requirement is a permanent finding and cannot be fixed. An appropriate mitigation for the system must be implemented but this finding cannot be considered fixed.
Rule.rationale: RHEL6 does not support this requirement.

check.check-content: This is a permanent finding.

Rule.title: Guidance Does Not Meet this Requirement Due to Impracticality or Scope
Rule.description: This requirement is NA. No fix is required.
Rule.rationale: The guidance does not meet this requirement. The requirement is impractical or out of scope.

check.check-content: RHEL6 cannot support this requirement without assistance from an external application, policy, or service. This requirement is NA.

Rule.title: A process for prompt installation of OS updates must exist.
Rule.description: Procedures to promptly apply software updates must be established and executed. The Red Hat operating system provides support for automating such a process, by running the yum program through a cron job or by managing the system and its packages through the Red Hat Network or a Satellite Server.
Rule.rationale: This is a manual inquiry about update procedure.

check.check-content:
Ask an administrator if a process exists to promptly and automatically apply OS software updates. If such a process does not exist, this is a finding.
If the OS update process limits automatic updates of software packages, where such updates would impede normal system operation, to scheduled maintenance windows, but still within IAVM-dictated timeframes, this is not a finding.

metadata.title: Restrict Virtual Console Root Logins
metadata.description: Preventing direct root login to virtual console devices helps ensure accountability for actions taken on the system using the root account.

metadata.title: File /etc/cups/printers.conf Permissions
metadata.description: File permissions for /etc/cups/printers.conf must be 0644.

criteria.comment: packages samba-common and samba3x-common removed or /etc/samba/smb.conf configured correctly
